items.content_text:
Greenway Farm Garden Project. 
 Looking fantastic at Greenway Farm. 
 In 1988, a few local gardeners asked Dr. Spangler if they could plant a garden on his 160-acre farmland—what is now Greenway Farm Park. Delighted by the idea, he had his caretaker plow a plot so Hixson-area residents could grow their own food.
 In 1990, the City of Chattanooga purchased the land, and the Greenway Farm Gardeners continued under the North Chickamauga Conservatory. In 2025, they became an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit: the Greenway Farm Garden Project. Thanks to a lease with the City of Chattanooga Parks and Outdoors, their mission continues.
 The gardeners come from all around and share a passion for growing, teaching, and preserving both Greenway Farm Park and traditional gardening practices for future generations.
 Free educational sessions are offered on the second Saturday of every month from 10:00–11:00 AM, right next to the gardens.
 Visitors are welcome to stop by anytime, introduce themselves to the gardeners (who are happy to show people around), or contact the president, Sheri Steele, at sheristeele2020@gmail.com for open plots and information.  
 *Note their next class is Oct 10th focusing on winter prep for gardens*

items.content_text:
PARK IMPROVEMENTS | THANK YOU, HAMILTON COUNTY!
 Ooltewah Youth Association would like to give a big THANK YOU to the Hamilton County Tennessee Parks & Recreation Department for their continued partnership and investment in our community.
 Two recent projects are great examples of what can happen when the County and OYA work together:
 ⚾ East Hamilton Park
 OYA was fortunate to purchase the large baseballs that were previously displayed outside the Chattanooga Lookouts stadium. Hamilton County Parks & Recreation helped get them set in place at East Hamilton Park, giving these pieces of local baseball history a new home. We hope they become a fun part of the park that players and families enjoy for many years to come.
 🔨 Standifer Gap Park – Field 3
 The fencing on Field 3 has also been replaced. Hamilton County provided the funding for the new fencing, while OYA managed the project from start to finish.
 These improvements are about more than baseball fields and fences. They are investments in places where kids play, families gather, and memories are made.
 We truly appreciate Hamilton County Parks & Recreation and their willingness to partner with OYA as we continue improving the facilities that serve our kids and our community.
 Thank you for investing in Ooltewah and in youth sports!
 #OYA #OoltewahYouthAssociation #HamiltonCounty #ParkImprovements #YouthSports #Ooltewah #CommunityPartnership

Today, UTC celebrated 140 years of creating opportunity through education. 💙💛
 During her first State of the University address, Chancellor Lori Mann Bruce reflected on UTC’s 140-year history, highlighted the people and accomplishments shaping the University today, and shared a vision for where UTC is headed next.
 From student success and hands-on learning to nationally recognized research, community engagement and nearly $500 million in capital projects, the University is building on its purpose while preparing for the future.
 Following the address, the UTC community came together on Terrell Owens Way to celebrate 140 years with the UTC Alma Mater, a ceremonial birthday cake cutting with Chancellor Bruce and UT System President Randy Boyd, and an afternoon of birthday fun. 🎂🎉
 Here’s to 140 years of Mocs making an impact and to the generations still to come.
 🔗  Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/state-of-the-university-2026-140-ye…/

items.content_text:
So excited to see Chattanooga named one of the five best trail towns in America, alongside four other amazing destinations.
 We're grateful to our team members who work tirelessly to keep Chattanooga at the forefront of writers' and editors' minds as they curate these lists!
 Read more: https://www.visitchattanooga.com/…/outside-magazine-names-…/ 
 #Chattanooga #travelandtourism | Tennessee Vacation | Outside Magazine
Outside Magazine named Chattanooga one of the five best trail towns in America.
 The other four are Bend, Boulder, Marquette, and Mill Valley. Mill Valley has about 14,000 people. Chattanooga has 194,000 (Metro pop is way bigger). Being ten minutes from a trailhead is normal when you live in a town of 14,000. It is not normal here, and that is the whole story.
 We have never pitched Chattanooga as a city with great outdoor access. That framing puts nature somewhere else. Here it is not somewhere else. The mountains and the river got here first, and the city had to work around them.
 Here is how it came together, because these stories do not assemble themselves.
 Erin McGrady at Authentic Story Co. came to us looking for insider knowledge, not a press kit. Ava Rymer went straight to the running community and got Peter Hagemeyer at Fast Break Athletics to answer eight questions on a brutal deadline. Susan Harris connected us to Ginny Smith at Bad Beard Events, who is directing the 2027 UTMB Ultra-Trail Chattanooga (June 4–6, 2027). 
 “What’s unique about Chattanooga is that you can be standing downtown and within 10 or 15 minutes be at the base of Lookout Mountain via the Riverwalk, on Raccoon Mountain, at Stringer’s Ridge, or up on Signal," Smith says. 
 Congratulations to everyone who has spent decades building and protecting the trails that made this true. 
 Chattanooga Tourism Co. Chattanooga Parks and Outdoors City of Chattanooga - Government

 We can think of no person more deserving to be the first East Ridge citizen recognized under the statute than Councilman Jacky Cagle.  A lifetime of service.  A lasting legacy in #EastRidgeTN. 🤍

items.content_text:
Switzerland has one of the most prosperous, competitive and innovative economies in the world, thanks to strong institutions and prudent macroeconomic management.
 Yet high trade tensions and geopolitical uncertainty are creating new challenges. To sustain growth and ensure long-term fiscal sustainability, ambitious reforms will be key.
 Policy priorities include:
 ➡️ Linking future retirement age increases to gains in life expectancy
 ➡️ Improving healthcare efficiency through stronger coordination across cantons
 ➡️ Expanding public spending reviews beyond subsidies
 ➡️ Increasing the low value-added tax rate to support compliance with the debt brake
 These steps can help ease the pressure on public finances resulting from ageing populations, climate change and increased defence spending.
 Read the #OECD Economic Survey of Switzerland https://oe.cd/6HY

items.title: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the G20 area grew by 0.7% in the second quarter of 2026, slightly down from 0.8% in the...
items.content_text:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the G20 area grew by 0.7% in the second quarter of 2026, slightly down from 0.8% in the previous quarter. 
 Among G20 economies, the contraction in Saudi Arabia deepened, with GDP falling by 4.8% in Q2 2026, following a 1.4% decline in Q1, this mainly reflected a sharp decrease in oil activities. 
 By contrast, growth rebounded strongly in Mexico, with GDP increasing by 1.4% in Q2 after contracting by 0.3% in Q1, and remained strong in Indonesia, at 1.3% (similar to Q1). Growth also strengthened in Türkiye, from 0.3% to 1.1%, and in Canada, from 0.1% to 0.8%, while it picked up slightly in Australia, from 0.3% to 0.4%. In France, GDP was unchanged in Q2, following a contraction of 0.2% in Q1.  
 Learn more: https://brnw.ch/21x5Hfv | #OECDstats

Getting to class can be one of the most routine parts of a student’s day, but the hassle of parking, navigating Chattanooga’s heat and long walks across campus can throw that routine off. For students looking to ease these burdens, UTC offers the Mocs Express shuttle as a convenient, safe way to get around campus free of charge. 🚌 
 The Mocs Express shuttle operates a regular 13-hour route Monday through Friday, with a special Friday evening route for students to enjoy. Starting at Engel Stadium, the Mocs Express runs through campus and the neighboring streets for a complete loop of less than 30 minutes. Once the bus returns to its starting point, the route restarts.

items.content_text:
It is with profound sadness that the City of East Ridge announces the passing of Councilman Jacky Cagle.
 For nearly half a century, Jacky dedicated his life to serving the people of East Ridge first as a City employee from 1976 to 2010 and later as a member of the East Ridge City Council from 2014 to 2026.
 Through every chapter of his service, Jacky worked to leave East Ridge stronger and better than he found it.  His dedication to our community, the relationships he built, and the legacy he leaves behind will not be forgotten.
 “We are overwhelmed by the loss of Council Member Jacky Cagle,” said Mayor Brian Williams.  "He was a friend and someone who truly cared about East Ridge and the people who call our community home.
 The City of East Ridge extends its heartfelt thoughts and prayers to his wife, Donna, and their family during this incredibly difficult time.  May they find strength and comfort in knowing how much Jacky meant to so many people and how deeply he will be missed."
 Information regarding arrangements will be shared once it has been finalized and made publicly available by the family.
 A lifetime of service.  A lasting legacy in #EastRidgeTN! 🤍

UTC welcomed 11,809 students for fall 2026, the second-highest enrollment in the University’s 140-year history and set an all-time high for graduate enrollment.
 Graduate enrollment reached 1,749 students, a 5% increase over the previous record of 1,664 set last year. The graduate population includes more than 550 professional and research doctoral students, reflecting UTC’s expanding research enterprise and portfolio of advanced academic programs.
 “Our enrollment numbers show that the momentum at UTC continues,” said Chancellor Lori Bruce.

items.title: The OECD unemployment rate was at 4.9% in July 2026, its lowest level in a year. The number of unemployed individuals in...
items.content_text:
The OECD unemployment rate was at 4.9% in July 2026, its lowest level in a year.
 The number of unemployed individuals in the OECD fell to 34.7 million, the lowest level in a year.
 In July 2026, unemployment rates remained steady at 6.1% in the European Union and 6.4% in the euro area.
 Japan, Mexico and Korea maintained unemployment rates below 3.0%, the lowest among OECD countries.
 By contrast, Finland and Spain reported double-digit unemployment rates, with Finland nearly 5.0 percentage points (p.p.) above its historic low from almost two decades ago.
 Learn more:  https://brnw.ch/21x5G3h | #OECDstats

A great example of teamwork — and giving something a second life! ⚽️🌱
 Hamilton County Parks & Recreation was proud to partner with Chattanooga Football Club and the City of Chattanooga to help relocate sod originally used at Erlanger Park for a professional soccer match to its new home at East Lake Park.
 Our Parks crew helped haul and transport the grass to East Lake, where it could be reused to refresh the soccer area and improve playing conditions for the community.
 Instead of seeing a valuable resource go to waste, partners came together, rolled up their sleeves and found a way to put it right back to work for local families and athletes.
 We love seeing collaboration like this turn into a visible community improvement. The before ➡️ during ➡️ after transformation speaks for itself!
 Thank you to Chattanooga Football Club, the City of Chattanooga and everyone who helped make it happen.
 #HamiltonCountyParks #EastLakePark #ChattanoogaFC #CommunityPartnership #Teamwork #ChattanoogaTN #ParksAndRecreation
From the professional pitch to the community field! 
 The East Lake Park soccer area is looking great after a much-needed refresh!
 The sod originally used at Erlanger Park for a CFC professional soccer match was donated and given a second life at East Lake Park, helping us repair and improve the playing area for the community.
 This is a great example of what can happen when partners work together. CFC, the City of Chattanooga, and Hamilton County Parks & Recreation came together to turn used sod into a valuable community improvement.
 From before ➡️ during ➡️ after, the transformation speaks for itself!
 Thank you to everyone who helped make this partnership possible and helped bring better playing conditions to East Lake Park.

 Captain Phillips spearheaded the project, which is now the largest fully accessible playground in the Chattanooga area. A custom farm-themed playground was designed with universal accessibility at its core, ensuring children of all physical abilities can play together without barriers.
 Designed for ages 2–12, the park features fully ramped play structures, wheelchair-accessible carousel elements, adaptive swings, sensory enrichment stations, and seamless rubber surfacing for barrier-free play.
 It’s a model project for excellence for other designs like it at other parks and playgrounds!

Heads up, Collegedale!
 On October 7, 8, and 10, you may notice a couple of small cameras along the Wolftever Greenway, near Veterans Memorial Park. No need for concern — these are temporary pedestrian and bicycle counters, not surveillance devices.
 What's happening: The City of Collegedale is working with the Hamilton County Regional Planning Agency (RPA) and the Chattanooga-Hamilton County/North Georgia Transportation Planning Organization (MPO) to gather data on how our community uses the greenway.
 Why it matters: This data helps the City pursue grant funding to extend and enhance our greenway trail system, supporting our efforts to expand walkability and alternative travel options throughout Collegedale.
 We appreciate our residents helping make Collegedale an even more connected, walkable community! 
 Questions or concerns about the count period or device placement? Contact us at (423) 396-3135.

HCSO, TBI, Homeland Security Investigations Joint Investigation Unveils Local Business Was a Cover for a Prostitution Operation
 Hamilton County, TN – On the late morning of September 9, 2026, a joint undercover investigation involving the HCSO Criminal Investigations Unit, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI), and Homeland Security Investigations uncovered a woman soliciting prostitution at S-Lucky Spa, address 7794 East Brainerd Road, Suite 110. 
 The business was found on a website known for advertising prostitution, and an investigation into the business confirmed the spa was being used as a cover for prostitution. An undercover operation was conducted alongside the execution of a search warrant for the business. Authorities arrested a female employee, identified as Wei Guang Han, during the operation, and evidence identified as being used for the furtherance of crime to include money, was seized during the investigation.
 Han was transported to the Hamilton County Jail & Detention Center and faces the following charge: 
 • Prostitution
 Direct any questions to the TBI and Homeland Security Investigations. View the TBI's news release here: https://tbinewsroom.com/…/statewide-operation-addresses-il…/.

At this year’s “Three Stars of Tennessee Award,” Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, State Senator Becky Duncan Massey, Department of Safety and Homeland Security Commissioner Jeff Long, and Deputy Commissioner Greg Mays recognized Hamilton County Deputy Landon Faulkner and five other first responders who lost their lives or suffered a career-ending injury while in the line of duty.
 Deputy Faulkner passed away on April 10, 2026, two days after his patrol vehicle collided with a disabled truck on a highway. Faulkner is remembered for his devotion to his family, dedication to law enforcement, and commitment to public service.
 His award was received by his wife, Megan; his father, Chad; and Hamilton County Sheriff Austin Garrett, in solidarity with the Faulkner family and the HCSO.
